figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Biosynthetic pathway of paclitaxel and related taxane compounds.
The mainstream towards paclitaxel is shown with a light yellow background. Compounds transiently accumulated in the early culture phase (1–3 days after
induction) of Taxus cell suspension cultures are highlighted with green and a single asterisk. Compounds accumulated in the middle to late culture phase (later
than 10 days) are highlighted with orange and double asterisks. Each biosynthetic step is shown in red letters in a simpliﬁed name (AT acetylation; BzT, benzoyl-
transferase; DBAT, 10-DAB 10-acetyltransferase; NDPPT, N-debenzoylpaclitaxel pentanoyltransferase; OH, hydroxylation; PTT, NDPTT, N-debenzoylpaclitaxel
tigloyltransferase). Two key branching points are indicated with circled numbers. Solid arrows show the reaction step in which the biosynthetic enzymes are
reported, and dotted arrows are putative conversion steps. *Position of acetoxy residues of hexaacetoxytaxadiene, deacetylbaccatin IV, and 1-
hydroxydeacetylbaccatin I is an example.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Snapshots of time course metabolomics monitoring of taxane compounds accumulated in the culture medium.
The representative 3D chromatograms of LC–MS analysis at 2 days (a), 19 days (b), and 40 days (c) are shown. The original time-lapse animation of the 3D chro-
matogram is shown in Movie 1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Accurate MS measurement of representative peaks under 100 lM methyl jasmonate induction conditions.
(a) Quantitative progression of compound accumulation as MS signal count of major ion. Graph colour indicates accumulation stages as green, light green,
orange, and red for earlier to later. Yellow indicates paclitaxel derivatives with accumulation peak around 2 weeks after induction.
(b) Component analysis estimating the type of detected ions and their annotation.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. NMR analysis of the fractionated culture product.
(a, b) 2D HSQC NMR spectra of water-soluble (a) and water-insoluble (b) fractions obtained from the product mixtures at 6, 14, and 47 days after induction. The
signals of the major product, 9-dihydrobaccatin III, are highlighted in pink.
(c) 2D HSQC NMR spectra of the water-soluble fraction obtained from the product mixture at 47 days after induction, superimposed on the spectra of taxane
standards. The structural identity of the major product as 9-dihydrobaccatin III was conﬁrmed by comparing the signal patterns with those of the standards and
the reported NMR data of 9-dihydrobaccatin III (Ketchum, Tandon, et al., 1999; Zamir et al., 1992, 1995).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Co-expression network in the transcriptome around taxadiene synthase.
(a) A local part of the co-expression network probed with a homologous contig of taxadiene synthase (yellow circle, accession number U48796). The full-scale
image is shown in Figure S3. Light pink circles indicate transcriptome contigs with membrane transporter-like annotations, and the NPF transporters are
highlighted with dark pink. The light blue circle indicates genes related to paclitaxel biosynthesis. Labels indicate contig IDs.
(b) GO enrichment analysis of the extracted contigs in the co-expression network. GO terms in the molecular function category with more than ﬁvefold enrich-
ment are shown. GOs indicating NPF transporters, membrane transporters, paclitaxel pathway, and taxadiene synthases are highlighted in dark pink, light pink,
light blue, and yellow, respectively. Grey bars represent the P-value.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Paclitaxel sensitivity of yeast expressing Taxus NPF transporter genes.
Paclitaxel-sensitive yeast strain MGY2150 was transformed with yew NPF transporter genes, and growth was examined in YPD plate (a) and liquid medium (b)
containing 1 lM paclitaxel.
(a) Colony growth was more suppressed in TmNPF2.1, TmNPF2.2, and TmNPF2.3 expressing strains than in controls. Strain MGY1872 has a normal tubulin
gene, which is tolerant to paclitaxel. Bar represents 1 cm.
(b) The TmNPF2.1-expressing strain showed suppressed growth in YPD liquid medium containing 1 lM paclitaxel (PTX), but the TmNPF2.2- and TmNPF2.3-
expressing strains did not, probably due to the control. Orange and blue plots show growth curves in YPD medium with and without 1 lM paclitaxel. Due to the
OD monitor’s speciﬁcation, any measurement beyond 8.88 is recorded as the limit value.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Conversion of 10-DAB to baccatin III in yeast culture.
(a) Baccatin III production in yeast culture analysed by LC–MS. The DBAT gene was introduced into a yeast strain W303-1A in the presence (top) or absence
(middle) of TmNRT2.1 in the plasmid vector pESC-URA carrying the constitutive promoters TEF and PMA. The bottom panel shows a negative control using the
W303-1A without plasmid. The arrows indicate the substrate 10-DAB and the product baccatin III.
(b) Baccatin III production under variable pH conditions.
(c, d) Time course analysis of decreasing 10-DAB substrate (c) and accumulating baccatin III (d) in the culture with variable initial substrate. The concentration of
10-DAB was 12.5–200 lM. MS signals at m/z 545.2 at Rt 6.1 min and 587.2 at Rt 7.0 min peak were counted as speciﬁc signals of 10-DAB and baccatin III, respec-
tively. Bars represent the standard deviation of ﬁvefold (b) and fourfold (c, d) biological replicates.
